parts.title: They Put Him In An Interrogation Chair

series.summary: Rentarou visits a girlfriend's enormous family mansion and discovers the visit is actually a test: a hidden interrogation chair rises out of the floor and he is strapped in under a lie-detector lamp, where the first question is whether he really likes her. He answers honestly, she screams that he is lying, and the machine keeps judging him.

segments.voiceover_text: The mansion floor splits open and something rises out of it. It is a red interrogation chair. Rentarou came here to meet a girlfriend's family. Nobody told him he would be the one on trial. The blonde girl with the green ribbons clings to his shoulder, scarlet to the ears, and says nothing useful at all.

Strapped in, lamp glowing over his head, he gets the only question that matters. Does he like her. She panics and insists it is a perfectly normal thing to ask. He says yes. She shrieks that he is lying. The lamp does not blink. It never had to.

parts.title: He Ran Past A Wall Of Guards

series.summary: The interrogation grinds on and stops being funny. Cornered in the chair, Rentarou stops defending himself and starts pushing back, and later, on a dark swing set, the blonde girl admits she cannot keep waiting on him. Back in the mansion hall he makes a decision and bolts straight through her mother's security line.

segments.voiceover_text: The questions keep coming and the room stops laughing. He is pinned in that chair, arguing his own feelings out loud to strangers. Every answer becomes evidence against him. He is humiliated. He answers anyway, because folding here means losing her.
Later, on a dark swing set, her bravado is gone. She says she cannot keep waiting for him. That is the part that hurts. She is not angry. She is tired.
So he stops negotiating. Back in the hall, with her mother watching from the throne, he runs straight at a wall of guards. Hands grab him. He does not stop. He has to reach her first.

parts.title: The Promise She Made In The Rain

series.summary: The story drops into the memory the whole mansion standoff is built on: a crimson-haired girl in tears promising she will always stay with him. The promise does not hold. She breaks away, and the night ends with her on the ground and him left waiting at a door he is not allowed through.

segments.voiceover_text: Then the story goes back. A crimson-haired girl, lit blue by the dark, is crying so hard she can barely speak. She says she loves him. She promises she will always be with him. It is the sweetest line in the episode and it lands like a warning.

Because promises like that get tested. She tells him it is fine, she will wait, and then she is gone from the frame and down on the pavement, tears streaking sideways. He is left at a doorway that is not his to open, told to clear off.

parts.title: The Lie Detector Versus A Hot Spring

series.summary: Back in the present the interrogation turns cold: a blinding lamp, a calm woman studying him, and no sympathetic audience. Meanwhile the rest of the girlfriends are relaxing in the family hot spring, and the moment someone orders the two of them sorted out, the bath becomes an emergency.

segments.voiceover_text: Back under the lamp, the comedy drains out of it. The light is blinding and the woman questioning him does not raise her voice once. That is somehow worse. He is losing this.
One room over, his other girlfriends are soaking in the family hot spring, completely at peace. Then the order comes down: sort those two out. Peace over.
A phone comes up with the words emergency escape on the screen. Nobody in that bath is going to stay out of this. The one thing they are all worried about is him.

series.summary: The ordeal ends not with a verdict but with a corridor at night, a towel, and two people too embarrassed to look at each other. The apologies pile up, the panic burns out, and the series closes on the quiet thing the mansion spent all day trying to disprove.

segments.voiceover_text: Afterwards, a dark corridor. She is in a hoodie, he is steaming red from the bath, and neither of them can finish a sentence. She hands him a towel like it is a peace treaty.
Then it breaks. She throws her arms up, wails, kicks the air, apologises about six times in a row. He apologises back. Two futons, two faces glowing pink, nobody looking anybody in the eye.
And by morning the noise is gone. A girl with dark red hair is asleep against his shoulder, breathing slow. No chair, no lamp, no guards. Nobody needed a machine to confirm this part.
